prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, opening the field of moire flat-band quantum matter

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize for B021 to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. After the first round the case rests on three points that nobody has contested. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a quantitative prediction, made from band-structure reasoning, of a specific twist angle at which the bands flatten. The 2018 experiments found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle. And the twist angle has become a general control parameter for interaction strength against bandwidth, now used well beyond graphene. As a theorist who works with electronic-structure methods, I regard a result that is predicted, then found at the predicted place, and then reproduced by many laboratories as the strongest kind of evidence we get. The chair's question on citation wording has a direct answer: the citation I propose is built on the flat-band prediction and on the observed phases, and it says nothing about the pairing mechanism, so the unresolved mechanism does not enter what we would be certifying.
statement.case_against: The honest weakness is timing. The 2018 experiments are eight years old, and the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated; a committee that wants the interpretation settled should prefer B030 or B024. I now weigh this more heavily than in round 1, because members with several different first choices raised it independently. My answer is that we would be honouring a platform and its reproducible phenomenology, which are not in doubt, and not an explanation, which is how earlier prizes have often treated discoveries whose theory lagged behind. I do not claim this fully removes the objection. The credit is also incomplete: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, and the groups of Dean, Young, Yazdani and Efetov, and earlier moire band-structure work, fall outside any three-name set. I accept that cost and regard it as a consequence of the limit of three, not as evidence that the credited names are wrong.

responses.point: The chair argues that B030 rests on results stable for fifteen years, that B021 is only eight years old with a debated superconducting mechanism and uncredited parallel experiments, and that he would not oppose B021 later.
responses.response: The difference in maturity between B030 and B021 is real and I will not argue it away. Where I differ is on what it implies. For B030 the sharper problem to me is credit. If the citation names the quantum spin Hall prediction and observation, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp are defensible, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that told the experimenters to use HgTe sits outside, and Hasan's 3D work would make a broader citation about topological insulators look incomplete. For B021 the three names map onto the decisive steps, which are the prediction and continuum model, and the 2018 discovery. The 2016 overlap is a second consideration. I accept that Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz did not cover time-reversal-invariant insulators, so I do not call B030 too close, but I do think a second topological prize within ten years is a cost that B021 does not carry. I have kept B030 as my first alternative and would support it if the committee finds the credit can be settled.

responses.point: Kroll keeps B024 first, with a clean Katori-Ye credit and applications in relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants, and notes that the redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
responses.response: I agree with you that B024 has the cleanest credit and a thoroughly confirmed result, and that it is not merely a precision increment. I have added B024 to my alternatives for that reason. I still put B021 above it for the reason I gave in round 1, which is the difference between a capability and a new regime of physics. You list the payoff as not yet arrived; for B021 the payoff, a new family of correlated and topological phases that can be tuned in one device, has arrived and has been reproduced widely. I would also say that B024 has a timing problem of its own, since the redefinition of the second, which would make the case decisive, has not happened. We should treat the two symmetrically and not demand more of B021.

responses.point: Lindroth says the superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is less mature than the clock, and doubts that breadth of follow-on activity is merit by itself.
responses.response: I accept the second point, and I will not rely on breadth as an argument. Many papers do not make a prize, and some of the activity reflects open questions. What I rely on is narrower. The magic angle was predicted before the experiment, the experiment found the phases at that angle, and the correlated insulator in particular has been reproduced in several laboratories with the same twist-angle dependence. That is a falsifiable prediction that held, and it does not depend on the count of follow-up papers. On maturity, I agree the superconductivity is less settled than a lattice clock, and that is why the citation avoids a mechanism. You are better placed than I am to judge how new the lattice clock is against the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and I take your distinction seriously.

responses.point: Danielsson says B021 is as clean as B030 in theory-to-experiment structure but is held back by the lack of an agreed mechanism, and prefers the trio Kane, Mele and Molenkamp.
responses.response: I agree that the trio is better than a Kane-Molenkamp pair, which would be tidy on paper but would split the original proposal. Mele's role in it is equal to Kane's. If the committee goes to B030, I would support your three names. Where we still differ is how much a missing mechanism should count. The Z2 classification is a complete theoretical statement that experiment confirmed, while magic-angle graphene is a younger experimental field. My view is that for a discovery prize the standard is whether the phenomenon is robust and attributable, and I think it is. I do concede that B030 is the lower-risk option, and if the committee wants the lowest-risk outcome, that is the one to choose.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B021 first and raises the possibility of a two-part prize pairing a condensed-matter achievement with B024 or B030, and concedes that eight years is short.
responses.response: I considered the two-part configuration, since I mentioned B024 as a possible second part myself. The limit of three people makes it unattractive. B021 needs all three names, so a second part would force me to cut one of them and split the authorship of the prediction, or to give B024 only a single credited name, which would split Katori and Ye. For B030 the same arithmetic applies. I would prefer a single, well-defined prize over two parts that each lack a principal. I share your concession on timing and I read it as the main risk to our own first choice.

uncertainties: Whether eight years and an unsettled superconducting mechanism are acceptable for a discovery prize when B030 and B024 offer longer confirmation records.
Whether leaving out Yuan Cao and the independent experimental groups weakens the three-name credit.
Whether the credit for B030 can be resolved among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan so that it overtakes B021 on the merits.
How new optical lattice clocks are relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, which I cannot judge as well as the atomic physicists on the committee.
My dates and priority details come from memory of the literature and have not been verified against sources in this exercise.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B021, B030 or B024. My documented connections are my doctoral supervisor, Los Alamos, co-authors of my books and colleagues in Uppsala, and none is a credited name. I previously disclosed professional proximity to B019 because I use density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory. I no longer list B019 as an alternative, so this disclosure is unchanged in substance and is retained for the record.
